title: TB skin test (Mantoux and Diaskintest)
what: A drop of a special substance is injected into the skin of your forearm. After 3 days, the doctor checks for redness or a raised bump and measures it. Diaskintest is a similar skin test used in some countries.
why: To check for tuberculosis in children and adults: yearly at schools and kindergartens, after contact with someone with TB, or for medical certificates.
duration: the injection takes 1 minute; the check is usually after 72 hours
tell_doctor: If you have a fever, a cold, or a flare-up of an illness right now
If you have allergies or skin conditions
If you had a recent vaccine
If your child is ill, tell the doctor in advance. The test may be postponed

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: No special prep. You can eat as usual.

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The test is done when you are well. With a cold, it is usually postponed. Ask your doctor.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Wear a sleeve that is easy to pull up to the elbow.

bring: Your referral, if you have one
steps: You sit and rest your forearm on a table
A thin needle puts a drop just under the top layer of skin
A small bubble forms on the skin
You are given a day to come back and show your arm
feel: You can tell a child ahead of time: it will be quick and pinch a little
after: Until the check, do not wet or scratch the spot, and do not cover it with a bandage or put cream on it
After 72 hours, the doctor measures the reaction with a ruler
You get the result right at the check
red_flags: Strong swelling of the arm, blisters, or red streaks from the spot: see a doctor before the check day

faq.q: Can the test spot get wet?
faq.a: Better not. Do not rub it, scrub it, or soak it until the check. A few drops of water are usually fine.

faq.q: How is Diaskintest different from Mantoux?
faq.a: Diaskintest does not react to the BCG vaccine, so it shows TB infection more precisely.

reminders.text: TB skin test tomorrow. If you have a fever or a cold, call the clinic.
